🔀 **F-2656-1 — IN A PAIRED POSITIVE/NEGATIVE CONTROL, *AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE ARMS* IS ITSELF THE BROKEN-INSTRUMENT SIGNAL — YOU NEED NOT KNOW WHICH ARM IS RIGHT (measured s2656, LIVE ON MYSELF, on the RT-01 salt check).** F-2609-1 makes the salt check step 0 of any mint, and its whole design is a pair: re-mint a banked rotation with the REAL salt (must reproduce) and with a WRONG one (must not). 📊 **MEASURED: my first probe returned `0/NaN seeds reproduce | id false | opensAt false | closesAt false` for the REAL salt AND for a deliberately wrong salt — identical verdicts on arms that are *built to disagree*.** The salt was fine; my probe had guessed the output shape, assuming a bare rotation object with an ARRAY of seeds where `rotation-mint.mjs` emits a `{rotations:[…]}` WRAPPER with `seeds` as an OBJECT keyed by contract id. Corrected against the real shape, the same subjects read **REAL `r2026w37` 6/6 · `r2026w38` 6/6 · WRONG `r2026w38` 0/6**, reproducing F-2609-1’s figures to the digit. ⚖️ **SEVERITY STATED HONESTLY AND DELIBERATELY NOT INFLATED: realised cost ZERO, caught in ONE step, NOT a false green, and no verdict was published — the salt IS correct and tomorrow’s RT-01 mint is de-risked a day early.** 🎯 **What earns it a row is the DIRECTION had the shape error been subtler: a probe that zeroed only the seed comparison would have read `REAL 0/6` and been believed, publishing *"the owner’s salt is WRONG"* two days before a mint — a false alarm about the one input this law forbids reading directly, whose prescribed response is an expensive desk STOP. A broken probe fails toward ALARM here, not toward silence.** 🔑 **AND A SECOND, SEPARATELY MEASURED HALF THAT SHARPENS F-2609-1’s OWN WORDING: THE METADATA IS SALT-INDEPENDENT. `id`, `opensAt` and `closesAt` derive from the WEEK, not the salt — measured, the WRONG-salt arm scored `id+opensAt+closesAt identical: TRUE` while its seeds scored `0/6`.** So a comparison that folds metadata in makes a genuinely failing check look partly right, and a fire that eyeballs *"id matches, the dates match"* gets a FALSE CONFIRMATION on a secret it cannot otherwise inspect. **F-2609-1 already says compare its SEEDS; this measures why that word is load-bearing — key the comparison on seeds ALONE.** ⛔ **AND A THIRD MEASURED HALF THAT SHARPENS IT AGAIN, TAKEN FROM THE CODE RATHER THAN FROM OBSERVATION: `rotation-mint.mjs:38-41` shows `salt` enters ONLY the `createHmac`, while `id`/`opensAt`/`closesAt` derive from the ISO week — so the metadata is salt-independent BY CONSTRUCTION. And a seed is `${prefix}-${id}-${digest}` where only the trailing 12 hex chars are the HMAC: MEASURED, `131` of `203` seed characters (**64.5%**) are IDENTICAL under a wrong salt (real `e1-the-claim-r2026w38-f94c101b7c67` vs wrong `e1-the-claim-r2026w38-39591ca84e20`, 22 of 34 leading chars shared), while whole-string equality correctly reads `0 of 6`. **So "compare the seeds" must mean STRING EQUALITY IN CODE — a fire scanning seeds by eye sees a familiar prefix and a matching week and stops reading before the only 12 characters that discriminate.** 🚫 **NO GUARD, and the restraint is INHERITED rather than re-argued: *"did a fire’s ad-hoc probe assume the right output shape?"* is unobservable to every battery — the same reason F-2567-1 declined one for a hand-typed clock, F-1669-1 for a filename read with the eyes and F-2599-1 for a `| tail`. The cure is the sentence you are reading, plus the note now standing at the RT-01 site.** 💡 **REUSABLE, and it is the rung BETWEEN this streak’s two newest instrument findings: F-2215-1 says assert your control PRODUCED something; F-2655-2 (one fire old) says two broken probes can corroborate each other into a confident false verdict, and warns that the standing defence — a second instrument — fails when both are yours.
